statements.status_notes: CVE-2023-31439 lets an attacker who controls a sealed journal file remove its seals, re-seal past entries with a later sealing key, and still pass journalctl --verify, because verification did not check that entries are sealed only with the key for their own epoch, as described in section 5.1 of https://github.com/kastel-security/Journald/blob/main/journald-publication.pdf . Upstream fixed this in systemd v255 with https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/3846d3aa292a6daa1916f667bdd79ebee9cb4ac4 from pull request 28885, whose message says it resolves CVE-2023-31439: journal_file_verify() now rejects a tag when an entry's realtime falls outside that tag's epoch. Every published build of this package is made from systemd 257.13 (Debian trixie 257.13-1~deb13u1), which contains that commit. Checked libsystemd-shared-257.so, which holds journal_file_verify(), in every published libsystemd-shared package on amd64 and arm64: each contains the fix's 'is too late with respect to tag' and 'is too early with respect to tag' checks. Debian rates it unimportant and its tracker still lists trixie as vulnerable: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2023-31439 .
